I have been working this land for 40 years. Nine mu is not much, but it is mine and I know every part of it. Let me think through what I will do this year.

Most of my land — about 6 mu — I keep in the wheat-maize rotation. I plant winter wheat in October after rotary-tilling the maize stubble in, then come June I harvest the wheat and get the maize in right away on the same ground. This system I have done my whole life. It is steady. The other 3 mu I put in cotton because cotton still fetches decent money at the gin and we need the cash, especially since a few of my children are in the city now and don't help at harvest as much.

For wheat, I will use an improved variety — the kind the seed station sells. Nothing fancy, just what has worked well these past several years. I apply the base fertilizer before planting: diammonium phosphate mixed with urea and a bit of potash. Then I topdress in spring at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before freezing to help roots, once at jointing, once at heading. Two sprays for weeds and disease. I expect around 420 jin per mu, which is about what I get most years.

For summer maize, I direct-seed hybrid seed right after wheat harvest — no time for ploughing in summer. I water twice if the rains are light. Maize does not need as much hand attention as wheat. I count on 500-550 jin per mu.

For cotton on the 3 mu, I plough deep in spring. Cotton needs good roots. I use an improved Bt variety — much fewer bollworm sprays than the old days, but I still spray 4-5 times for aphids and other pests. Cotton drinks a lot, so I irrigate 3-4 times from the well. Yields maybe 250 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I will not change much this year. At 65, I am not going to experiment.
